```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
options(error = rlang::entrace, rlang_backtrace_on_error = "full")
library(tidyverse)
plants <- read.csv("tabular_data/Saanich_Tracheophyta_ultimate-catalogue_2026-08-20-selected-labels.csv")
plant.summary <- read.csv("tabular_data/Saanich_Tracheophyta_ultimate-summary_2026-08-20-prepared-taxa.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
  filter(inSummary == 1)
counts <- plant.summary %>% count(reportingStatus)
statusCount <- function (status) format(counts$n[counts$reportingStatus == status], big.mark = ",")
```

## The atlas of the Saanich Peninsula flora

To date, `r format(nrow(plant.summary), big.mark = ",")` vascular plant species have been recorded on the Saanich
Peninsula, drawing together `r format(nrow(plants), big.mark = ",")` records from historical collections, iNaturalist
observations and other sources. Each species falls into one of three groups:

* <button type="button" class="saanich-status-link" data-status="confirmed">Confirmed</button> (`r statusCount("confirmed")` species): reported historically and found again since 2000.
* <button type="button" class="saanich-status-link" data-status="unconfirmed">Historical</button> (`r statusCount("unconfirmed")` species): reported in the past but not recorded since 2000.
* <button type="button" class="saanich-status-link" data-status="new">Newly reported</button> (`r statusCount("new")` species): additions to the flora from recent reports.

These groups describe species. Choosing one shows every record of those species, old and recent, on the map and in the
list, and choosing it again returns to all of them.
The map shows where records are concentrated. Open *Filters* to narrow them by recorder, pick a plant from the list to
see only its records, or draw an area on the map. Open *Records* below the map for the details behind each
selection.
